svg.title: Direct rain catch when water supplies are limited
svg.desc: Working rain-catch diagram. Rainwater is not automatically safe. Catch rain directly into a suitable clean collector or the heat-safe pot that will be used for boiling. A sheet is used only when its maker confirms suitable drinking-water or liquid-food contact and it has no chemical, fuel, oil, coating, paint, animal-dropping or unknown residue. Keep the catch surface off soil and never remove shelter that a person needs. Reject catch exposed to ash, firefighting chemicals, fuel, oil, coolant, paint, pesticides, detergent or animal contamination. First runoff may remove loose dirt but cannot remove an unknown coating or chemical. One millimetre of rain on one square metre of horizontal footprint is at most one litre before losses. Caught rain still requires the complete treatment route.
svg.text: Rain catch when supplies are limited
RAINWATER IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY SAFE
Editorial confidence: 95% limits; 70% untested setup.
These figures describe wording—not safety or yield.
Caught rain still needs the complete treatment route.
DIRECT CATCH
Use a suitable clean collector
or the heat-safe boiling pot.
Never use a former chemical container.
Keep opening above soil splash.
SHEET CATCH — ONLY IF SUITABLE
Maker confirms water or liquid-food contact.
No coating, paint, fuel, oil or unknown residue.
One low drain point. Keep off soil.
REJECT THE CATCH
Ash or firefighting chemical;
fuel, oil, coolant, paint or detergent;
pesticide, animal droppings or unknown residue.
A first flush cannot fix a chemical or coating.
Never remove shelter that a person needs.
FIRST RUNOFF + YIELD
First runoff may remove loose dirt only.
1 mm rain × 1 m² horizontal footprint
= at most 1 L before losses.
Expect less from wind, slope, splash and leaks.
This calculation does not make water safe.
Treat caught rain with the rolling-boil card or an
exact reviewed product. Otherwise label it UNTREATED.
WORKING DRAFT — NOT FIELD-APPROVED
